---

Sam Bankman-Fried co-founded Alameda Research in 2017 and FTX in 2019 as a complement to it. Within two years of FTX's founding, over 80 investors provided approximately $2 billion in capital. In January 2022, FTX raised $400 million in a Series C round, boosting its valuation to $32 billion. That same year, FTX bought the naming rights for the Miami Heat's home arena and partnered with celebrities including Tom Brady, Gisele Bündchen, Steph Curry, Shaquille O'Neal, and Naomi Osaka.

CoinDesk published Alameda's balance sheet showing $14.6 billion in assets and $8 billion in liabilities as of June 30, 2022. Alameda's largest assets were $3.66 billion of 'unlocked FTT' and $2.16 billion of 'FTT collateral'. Alameda owned $5.82 billion in FTT tokens, which was 193% higher than the total FTT market cap of about $3 billion. Binance pulled out $2.1 billion equivalent of cash in BUSD and FTT, triggering a bank run on FTX.

FTX and Alameda filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in the U.S. in mid-November 2022. Sam Bankman-Fried resigned as CEO and John J. Ray III was appointed the new CEO. At The New York Times' DealBook Summit, Bankman-Fried stated he did not try to commit fraud and was shocked by the events. SBF was arrested in the Bahamas in December 2022, extradited to the U.S., and released on $250 million bail; his house arrest in Palo Alto was revoked in August following a diary leak accusation.

During the trial, John J. Ray III testified that FTX had virtually no internal controls or separateness and did not trust a single piece of paper. U.S. Attorney Damian Williams called the crimes the biggest financial fraud in American history. Gary Wang and Caroline Ellison pleaded guilty in December 2022 to federal charges and face civil penalties from the SEC and CFTC, planning to cooperate as witnesses. SBF pleaded not guilty in January to wire fraud, conspiracy to commit money laundering, and conspiracy to misuse customer funds, facing up to 115 years in jail if convicted on all charges. The FTX collapse was the first of many, with BlockFi filing for Chapter 11 in November 2022 and Genesis Global Trading filing in January.

Sam Bankman-Fried (SBF), the disgraced cryptocurrency entrepreneur accused of orchestrating the collapse of FTX, reportedly offered Donald Trump $5 billion to cancel his presidential re-run; no wire transfer was confirmed. SBF pleaded not guilty to seven charges of fraud and conspiracy in the Manhattan Federal Court trial.

Michael Lewis's book 'Going Infinite' is set to debut on the first day of SBF's trial. Lewis, introduced to SBF in early 2021 by a friend who wanted to back FTX, met SBF more than 100 times over the next two years. Lewis claimed SBF had $22.5 billion eighteen months earlier and was the richest person in the world under 30. 60 Minutes produced a segment featuring SBF shuffling cards and Lewis taking notes on a yellow legal pad. In a 60 Minutes interview, Lewis defended SBF's business practices, claiming FTX would have remained profitable without customer deposit runs.

FTX raised approximately $2 billion, including $1 billion in 2021, from backers including Sequoia, Temasek, and Tiger Global. To lend legitimacy, FTX secured marketing deals with Tom Brady ($55 million) and Steph Curry ($35 million). Anna Wintour contacted SBF via Zoom to sponsor her Met Costume Ball. FTX trading volume climbed to $15 billion per day. SBF also met with Mitch McConnell to fund Republican candidates offsetting Trump's influence.

The company's cryptocurrency valuations fell sharply after being based on speculation rather than banked value. SBF has been denied bail and is widely blamed by crypto investors for losses at Alameda Research and FTX. CEO Ayelet Noff of Sliced Brand criticized SBF, stating he lacked management experience, delayed crypto adoption by 1-2 years, and damaged the community. Financial discrepancies accumulated between FTX exchange and its sister company Alameda Research, leading to FTX's failure.

# See also

* [Sam Bankman-Fried trial: Opening statements and witness testimony](sam-bankman-fried-trial-opening-statements-and-witness.md) - A summary of the opening statements and initial witness testimony in the trial of Sam Bankman-Fried, covering the prosecution's allegations of fraud and the defense's arguments regarding startup risks and restitution.

### tech-news/sbf-s-trial-and-the-rise-and-fall-of-ftx.md

Title: SBF's trial and the rise and fall of FTX
Summary: This note covers the timeline from SBF's co-founding of Alameda and FTX in 2017-2019, through their massive growth and collapse in 2022, to his arrest, trial, and the broader industry fallout.

Sam Bankman-Fried co-founded Alameda Research in 2017 and FTX in 2019 as a complement to it. Within two years of FTX's founding, over 80 investors provided approximately $2 billion in capital. In January 2022, FTX raised $400 million in a Series C round, boosting its valuation to $32 billion. That same year, FTX bought the naming rights for the Miami Heat's home arena and partnered with celebrities including Tom Brady, Gisele Bündchen, Steph Curry, Shaquille O'Neal, and Naomi Osaka.

CoinDesk published Alameda's balance sheet showing $14.6 billion in assets and $8 billion in liabilities as of June 30, 2022. Alameda's largest assets were $3.66 billion of 'unlocked FTT' and $2.16 billion of 'FTT collateral'. Alameda owned $5.82 billion in FTT tokens, which was 193% higher than the total FTT market cap of about $3 billion. Binance pulled out $2.1 billion equivalent of cash in BUSD and FTT, triggering a bank run on FTX.

FTX and Alameda filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in the U.S. in mid-November 2022. Sam Bankman-Fried resigned as CEO and John J. Ray III was appointed the new CEO. At The New York Times' DealBook Summit, Bankman-Fried stated he did not try to commit fraud and was shocked by the events. SBF was arrested in the Bahamas in December 2022, extradited to the U.S., and released on $250 million bail; his house arrest in Palo Alto was revoked in August following a diary leak accusation.

During the trial, John J. Ray III testified that FTX had virtually no internal controls or separateness and did not trust a single piece of paper. U.S. Attorney Damian Williams called the crimes the biggest financial fraud in American history. Gary Wang and Caroline Ellison pleaded guilty in December 2022 to federal charges and face civil penalties from the SEC and CFTC, planning to cooperate as witnesses. SBF pleaded not guilty in January to wire fraud, conspiracy to commit money laundering, and conspiracy to misuse customer funds, facing up to 115 years in jail if convicted on all charges. The FTX collapse was the first of many, with BlockFi filing for Chapter 11 in November 2022 and Genesis Global Trading filing in January.

### tech-news/sbf-s-5b-offer-to-trump-and-ftx-s-rise-and-fall.md

Title: SBF's $5B offer to Trump and FTX's rise and fall
Summary: This note covers Sam Bankman-Fried's reported $5 billion offer to Donald Trump to cancel his presidential run, his background with Michael Lewis, FTX's marketing and trading growth, and the subsequent collapse and legal proceedings.

Sam Bankman-Fried (SBF), the disgraced cryptocurrency entrepreneur accused of orchestrating the collapse of FTX, reportedly offered Donald Trump $5 billion to cancel his presidential re-run; no wire transfer was confirmed. SBF pleaded not guilty to seven charges of fraud and conspiracy in the Manhattan Federal Court trial.

Michael Lewis's book 'Going Infinite' is set to debut on the first day of SBF's trial. Lewis, introduced to SBF in early 2021 by a friend who wanted to back FTX, met SBF more than 100 times over the next two years. Lewis claimed SBF had $22.5 billion eighteen months earlier and was the richest person in the world under 30. 60 Minutes produced a segment featuring SBF shuffling cards and Lewis taking notes on a yellow legal pad. In a 60 Minutes interview, Lewis defended SBF's business practices, claiming FTX would have remained profitable without customer deposit runs.

FTX raised approximately $2 billion, including $1 billion in 2021, from backers including Sequoia, Temasek, and Tiger Global. To lend legitimacy, FTX secured marketing deals with Tom Brady ($55 million) and Steph Curry ($35 million). Anna Wintour contacted SBF via Zoom to sponsor her Met Costume Ball. FTX trading volume climbed to $15 billion per day. SBF also met with Mitch McConnell to fund Republican candidates offsetting Trump's influence.

The company's cryptocurrency valuations fell sharply after being based on speculation rather than banked value. SBF has been denied bail and is widely blamed by crypto investors for losses at Alameda Research and FTX. CEO Ayelet Noff of Sliced Brand criticized SBF, stating he lacked management experience, delayed crypto adoption by 1-2 years, and damaged the community. Financial discrepancies accumulated between FTX exchange and its sister company Alameda Research, leading to FTX's failure.
